overall: The AG found violations where the Screening Committee shared finalist names in executive session, the School Committee discussed finalists in executive session, and notices omitted finalists' names; other allegations were declined, untimely, or not violations.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged numerous unspecified Open Meeting Law violations between November 2022 and March 2023 and asked the AG to audit all agendas and minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Because Paragraph 1 contains general allegations, we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the School Committee entered executive session on November 7, 2022 for negotiation strategy with no specific candidate identified, which was not a valid purpose.
allegations.key_passage: The complaint was filed on March 27 and is therefore untimely as to this issue.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 14, 2022 notice was insufficiently specific because it did not list a planned vote to form the Search Subcommittee.
allegations.key_passage: As the complaint was filed on March 27, it is untimely as to this issue.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the two Search Subcommittee members communicated outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: No specific communication is referenced and we will not perform an audit of the Search Subcommittee’s communications.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Screening Committee was a preliminary screening committee containing a quorum of the parent body, so its executive session under Purpose 8 was improper.
allegations.key_passage: Because the School Committee was the parent body of the Screening Committee, and fewer than a quorum of the members of the School Committee were appointed to the Screening Committee, there was no violation of the Open Meeting Law when the Screening Committee met in executive session under Purpose 8.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the January 24 notice was insufficiently specific because it did not list the vote to disband the Search Subcommittee.
allegations.key_passage: As the alleged violation occurred during the open meeting on January 24, the complaint, filed on March 27, was untimely as to this issue.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Screening Committee had to announce its finalists by name in open session after selecting them in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: There is no such requirement in the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Screening Committee improperly conveyed the names of selected finalists to the School Committee during executive session.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Screening Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when it provided the names of its selected finalists to the School Committee in executive session, because following the selection of finalists the Screening Committee no longer had a lawful basis for convening in executive session under Purpose 8.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the School Committee entered executive session on March 7 to discuss finalists the Screening Committee had recommended, which must occur in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Instead, the School Committee entered executive session to discuss the finalists, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the School Committee failed to take a roll call vote in executive session to advance all four semi-finalists to interviews.
allegations.key_passage: Any vote taken at an executive session must be recorded by roll call and entered into the minutes.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the March 16 and March 17 notices identified finalists only by letter designations rather than by name.
allegations.key_passage: Because the School Committee failed to include the names of the individuals, it violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Screening Committee failed to post notice of its March 6 meeting on its own separate website.
allegations.key_passage: The Screening Committee maintains, and the complainant has not disputed, that notice of the meeting was posted to the town’s official posting location.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a roll call vote was required to exit executive session and adjourn the Screening Committee's March 6 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: A roll call vote is not required to exit executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Screening Committee failed to report to the public, upon returning to open session, the action it took in executive session on March 6.
allegations.key_passage: The Screening Committee was not required to report on its actions in executive session and did not violate the Open Meeting Law in not doing so.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Screening Committee failed to conduct a roll call vote to enter or exit executive session on February 23.
allegations.key_passage: As it was filed March 27, it was untimely.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the violations were intentional because the School Committee had prior notice of OML violations.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, our prior determination cannot be relied upon to establish intent.

allegations.summary: Complainant requested additional remedies beyond those ordered, including voiding a superintendent hiring vote.
allegations.key_passage: We also decline to order other remedies requested by the complainant

remedy: Prepare and approve revised minutes of the March 7 executive session reflecting the names of finalists referenced, within 60 days, if finalists were discussed by name.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
remedy_passage: If the School Committee discussed finalists by name at its March 7 executive session, we order that the School Committee prepare and approve revised minutes of its March 7 executive session, reflecting the names of finalists referenced, within 60 days of this letter.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
